public_rationale: The evidence does not settle the claim either way. On the post date, 2025-05-27, TechCrunch reported that ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok offered voice chat, and that Anthropic was starting a beta voice mode for Claude in which users can chat about images (e2). OpenAI's May 2024 post says GPT-4o accepts text, audio, image and video input (e3). Google's December 2024 post says Gemini 2.0 Flash accepts image, video and audio input (e4). Both posts are from before the target period of 2025-04-01 to 2025-05-27, so they are context only. Meta's April 2025 Llama 4 post describes text and vision input and does not mention audio (e1). That is one leading family with no documented audio input. A 2025-05-31 report says Anthropic lists ElevenLabs as a text-to-speech subcontractor. The report infers from this that Claude may lack in-house audio models (e5). This concerns speech output and does not show what input Claude's model accepts. The packet has no evidence on DeepSeek. It does not show whether Grok took audio natively. So neither 'nearly all' leading models nor 'several' lacking an input type is shown. The answer also depends on whether product voice modes count.
limitations: The packet does not settle whether 'feature in' an LLM means native audio input to the model or voice input offered in the chatbot product.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: when the post went up on 2025-05-27, nearly all of the leading LLMs of the time (OpenAI GPT-4o, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, xAI Grok, DeepSeek) could take both image input and audio or spoken input.
'Basically every' allows one or two minor exceptions. It does not allow several of the leading model families to lack one of the two input types.

It is unclear whether 'feature in' an LLM means the model itself takes raw audio (native audio input) or that the company's chatbot product offers voice input, for example by turning speech into text first. Both readings are assessed here.

The claim describes an ongoing state with no named period. The target period is the model lineup current at posting, set as 2025-04-01 to 2025-05-27. Llama 4 came out in April 2025 and Claude 4 in May 2025.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that, as of late May 2025, nearly all leading LLMs or their chatbot products accepted both image and audio or voice input.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that, as of late May 2025, several leading LLM families lacked image input or audio input. Examples would be a flagship model documented as text-and-image only, or as text only.

evidence.locator: section on pre-training, paragraph on native multimodality
evidence.explanation: Meta describes Llama 4, its flagship model at the time, as combining text and vision only. Audio input is not mentioned. So one leading model family accepted images but not audio.

evidence.excerpt: A number of AI companies, including OpenAI, offer voice chat experiences for their respective chatbots. Google, for example, has Gemini Live, while xAI has Voice Mode for Grok.
evidence.explanation: On the post date, OpenAI, Google and xAI chatbots offered voice input, and Anthropic began rolling out voice mode. The same article says Claude voice users can chat about images. This supports the claim at the chatbot-product level.
